newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik peace talks end in partial accord -Tass.
newsitem.headline: Tajik peace talks end in partial accord -Tass.

text.p: The Tajik government and Islamic opposition signed a peace accord in Tehran on Sunday but failed to resolve all their differences at two weeks of talks in the Iranian capital, Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said.
Tass quoted Tajik Foreign Minister Talbak Nazarov, who signed the deal with deputy opposition leader Akbar Turadzhonsoda, as saying they had reached agreement on three of the four main points.
But they remained at odds over the government's demand that opposition groups disarm before returning to politics.

The two sides, who have been fighting a civil war for nearly five years, agreed to abandon rival claims and accusations over the conflict, to hold elections and to bring opposition figures into a transitional government. Tass gave no details.
Tens of thousands of people have been killed and many more displaced in fighting that followed the collapse of Soviet rule. Several previous ceasefire agreements have fallen apart.
Moscow-backed President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri agreed an outline accord at talks in neighbouring Afghanistan last month.

But tensions remain high in the rugged Central Asian state, where enmities are complicated by seething regional and clan rivalries. Some observers say the country risks descending into Afghan-style anarchy.
Thousands of troops from the Commonwealth of Independent States, led by Russians, have attempted to keep the peace. Several have been murdered in recent weeks.
